newsitem.title: ISRAEL: First International Bank Q1 net up.
newsitem.headline: First International Bank Q1 net up.

text.p: First International Bank of Israel Ltd.
(in thousands of shekels except per share)

First International said the sharp rise in its doubtful debt provision reflects the slowdown in the Israeli economy and its consequences for business activity as well as a worsening in the ability of a small number of clients to repay loans.
The increase in operating income was mainly due to increased activity in the Israeli capital markets.
Net return on equity in the first quarter rose to 9.3 percent from 8.0 percent a year earlier.
Credit to the public increased to 21.9 billion shekels from 19.2 billion a year earlier while deposits grew 14.5 percent in the same period to 26.7 billion shekels.
Total assets rose to 31.8 billion shekels from 27.4 billion in the first quarter of 1996.
Shareholders' equity rose to 2.1 billion shekels from 2.0 billion at the end of 1996.
Assets controlled by the bank's provident funds rose to 9.8 billion shekels from 9.5 billion at the end of 1996.
